brand.title: Follow the board. Build the stack.
brand.copy: A mobile-first weekly board built so you can train hard in the morning, hit skill work while you are fresh, and use the evening to restore mobility and flexibility without guesswork.

week.label: Apr 6 - Apr 12, 2026
week.focus: The last logged week was mostly missed, so this week is a clean restart rather than a catch-up block. Tuesday evening and Wednesday morning were also missed, so the rest of the week is now narrowed into a realistic bridge: reset tonight, recover the most important upper stimulus once, then finish the week without debt-stacking.
week.rhythm: Morning gym + skill Monday-Saturday, evening mobility + flexibility Monday-Saturday, Sunday full rest. Monday is a full training day, not a ramp-in placeholder.
week.automation: Nightly adjuster Mon-Sat at 10:00 PM, weekly reset Sunday at 9:00 PM

tracking.title: Log what you actually did.
tracking.copy: Use the shared session log after each morning or evening block. The nightly adjuster and Sunday planner both read it, and blank `Completed` cells are treated as not done, so mark completion, effort, joints, and any quick note while the session is still fresh.
fields: Notes: short context if something felt off
If `Completed` is blank, the automation treats it as not done

skillTracks.title: Push + balance
skillTracks.currentFocus: Build shoulder line, wrist tolerance, and overhead stacking while you are fresh in the morning instead of trying to do precision work when you are already tired.
milestones: Wall handstand hold stays stacked for 20-30s
Pike pressing strength improves without elbow irritation
Balance drills stop feeling like random survival reps

skillTracks.title: Pull + lever strength
skillTracks.horizon: Chest-to-bar -> muscle-up / tuck lever -> front lever
skillTracks.currentFocus: Own scap depression, active hang position, and explosive pull intent before chasing harder transitions.
milestones: Pull-ups stay crisp at the programmed submax volume
Chest-to-bar intent gets faster and cleaner
Front-lever prep can be added later without shoulder chaos

skillTracks.title: Core + compression
skillTracks.horizon: Hollow hold -> L-sit -> V-sit / press work
skillTracks.currentFocus: Train hollow body, hanging control, and compression as actual skill positions instead of just ab fatigue.
milestones: Hollow body hold stays solid for 20-30s
Hanging knee raise becomes strict and quiet
Compression work improves hip flexor control week to week

skillTracks.title: Leg control
skillTracks.horizon: Split squat -> pistol progression -> clean pistol squat
skillTracks.currentFocus: Keep lower-body skill work honest with ankle range, single-leg balance, and clean squat positioning.
milestones: Assisted pistol pattern feels balanced on both sides
Deep squat position gets more comfortable
Landing mechanics improve without knee irritation

days.title: Full-body foundation + handstand line
days.summary: Start the week with a full morning session that touches squat, press, pull, and hinge while you are fresh. Keep the volume honest and leave the gym feeling like you could still train again tomorrow.

morning.label: Morning / gym foundation
bullets: 8-10 min warm-up with hips, T-spine, shoulders, and wrists

skill.label: Morning skill block / handstand line
skill.copy: Do the skill work before the main lift while the shoulders and wrists are still fresh.
bullets: Wall shoulder taps or controlled weight shifts 2x6 per side

days.bodyweight: Run the displayed daily targets at the end of the morning session: 1 set push-ups, 1 set dips, 2 sets pull-ups, and 1 set squats. Stop with about 1-2 reps in reserve.
days.note: Monday is full on, but it is still a restart week. Strong and clean beats heroic and sloppy.
swaps: Front squat -> hack squat or leg press
Incline DB press -> machine chest press or weighted push-up
Chest-supported row -> cable row or 1-arm DB row

days.title: Lower strength + pistol pattern
days.summary: Take the first real lower-body day with enough volume to matter, then sharpen single-leg control while you are still switched on.

skill.label: Morning skill block / pistol pattern
skill.copy: Treat the single-leg work like skill practice, not like extra punishment after the squat.
bullets: Assisted pistol to box 3x4 per side

days.bodyweight: Run the displayed daily targets at the end of the morning session and keep the reps crisp, especially on dips and pull-ups.
days.note: Leave 1-2 reps in reserve on the squat and hinge.

evening.label: Evening / lower mobility + flexibility
bullets: Hamstring stretch or elephant walks 2 rounds

swaps: Back/front squat -> hack squat, leg press, goblet squat
RDL -> DB RDL or 45-degree back extension
Walking lunge -> reverse lunge or step-up

days.title: Missed morning / upper reset tonight
days.summary: Tuesday evening and Wednesday morning were both missed, so tonight is not a catch-up lift. Use it as a longer upper reset so Thursday morning can recover the main upper stimulus cleanly instead of turning the week into a scramble.

morning.label: Morning / missed upper session
bullets: Keep the evening focused on tissue quality and range
Use tonight to set up Thursday's bridge session

skill.label: Morning skill block / missed
skill.copy: The morning skill block was missed. Do not turn the evening mobility session into a second gym session to make up for it.
bullets: Stay with positions that restore shoulders, lats, T-spine, and wrists
Aim to feel fresher by the end of the evening than you did at the start

days.bodyweight: Skip the daily bodyweight work this morning and resume it tomorrow. Tonight stays recovery-only.
days.note: A missed morning does not earn an evening punishment session.

evening.label: Evening / long upper reset mobility + flexibility
bullets: Banded or doorway shoulder opener 2x30-45s per side
Wrist flexor and extensor stretch 2x30s per side

swaps: Wall lat stretch -> child’s pose side reach

days.title: Upper bridge + controlled explosive pull
days.summary: Thursday becomes the bridge day for the missed Wednesday upper session. Keep it at about 80-85% of the original upper volume so you recover the key stimulus once without making Friday and Saturday worse.

morning.label: Morning / upper bridge
bullets: 8-10 min shoulder, T-spine, and wrist warm-up

skill.label: Morning skill block / explosive pull bridge
skill.copy: Recover the missed pull-speed work, but do it with bridge-day discipline. Sharp reps matter more than volume here.

days.bodyweight: Run the displayed daily targets at the end of the morning session, but stay submaximal and trim to roughly 80-90% of the target if you still feel flat.
days.note: This is a bridge, not revenge training.

evening.label: Evening / shoulder, chest, and lat flexibility reset
bullets: Child's pose side reach 2x30s per side
Wrist flexor and extensor stretch 2x30s per side

swaps: Incline press -> DB bench or machine chest press
Chest-supported row -> cable row or 1-arm DB row

days.title: Athletic lower + agility
days.summary: The lower-power day slides to Friday after the Thursday upper bridge. Keep the jumps and change-of-direction work sharp, then trim one accessory if Thursday hit harder than expected.

morning.label: Morning / athletic lower
bullets: Line hops or ladder work 5 min
Sled push or bike sprint 5 rounds

skill.label: Morning skill block / lower-body control
skill.copy: Keep the lower-body skill side clean and springy. You are training landing quality and control, not chasing fatigue.
bullets: Assisted pistol to box 2x3 per side

days.bodyweight: Run the displayed daily targets at the end of the morning session, but keep the tempo smooth enough that Saturday still feels trainable.
days.note: Fast work stays fast. If you feel heavy, trim load before you trim intent.
swaps: Trap-bar deadlift -> kettlebell swing or heavy RDL
Bulgarian split squat -> reverse lunge or step-up
Sled push -> rower sprint or assault bike

days.title: Pull + posterior chain + balance-density closer
days.summary: Close the week with the planned pulling and posterior-chain work, then add a small push-and-balance touch so the midweek shuffle does not erase your second upper exposure entirely.

morning.label: Morning / pull + posterior chain closer
bullets: Incline DB press or weighted push-up 2x8

skill.label: Morning skill block / balance + compression
skill.copy: Keep the skill work positional and clean. The goal is to leave the week with quality positions, not with a fried nervous system.

days.bodyweight: Run the displayed daily targets at the end of the morning session. If you feel cooked by Saturday, keep the reps but slow the pace and stay submaximal.
days.note: Saturday is a clean closer, not a chance to make up every missed rep from the week.
swaps: RDL or trap-bar deadlift -> DB RDL or back extension
Neutral-grip pulldown -> ring row or band-assisted pull-up
Incline DB press -> weighted push-up or machine chest press

days.title: Full rest day
days.summary: No gym, no skill block, no catch-up. Let the system absorb the week so next Monday starts from actual recovery instead of accumulated guilt.

morning.label: Morning / off
morning.copy: No training. Walk if you want, but the day is for recovery.

skill.label: Skill block / off
skill.copy: Rest is part of the skill plan. It is how you come back sharp enough to practice the hard things properly.

days.bodyweight: Rest from the daily bodyweight work today.
days.note: A short easy walk is fine. Turning Sunday into a stealth training day is not.

evening.label: Evening / optional light stretch
evening.copy: Only do a few easy stretches if you feel stiff. This is not a second recovery workout.
